tools.name: changes_list
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks what changed in a store: chart moves, featuring, launches, delistings, metric moves or MCP changes, newest first with counts per type.
Do not use for a chart's full current order; use charts_get.

tools.name: new_list
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks which apps are new in a store since a time, by launch date or else the day each went live.
Do not use for rank or toolset changes; use changes_list.

tools.name: stores_get
tools.description:
Use this when you need stores, app counts, countries, freshness, charts or metrics. Pass store for chart names. guide returns a playbook's steps: weekly_brief (a store's week), competitor_watch (compare apps), audit_my_server (an MCP server's tools).
Do not use for rankings; use charts_get.

tools.name: charts_get
tools.description:
Use this when you need a chart now or at a past time, with movement and 1-based positions.
Do not use for a listing across charts; use listings_profile.

tools.name: leaderboards_get
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks which apps lead a store by a published number. claude: installs, popularity_score, trending_score, gh_stars; cursor: dir_installs, dir_stars.
Do not use for chart positions; use charts_get.

tools.name: scores_list
tools.description:
Use this when the user asks which apps are popular in a store over the last month: OpenApps Rank, a 28-day aggregate of its popularity charts, with tier and momentum.
Do not use for one day's chart order (charts_get) or published counts (leaderboards_get).

tools.name: listings_search
tools.description:
Use this when you need an app's ref from its name, its publisher, a brand it works with or what it does ("create jira ticket"); one row per app, best match first.
Do not use for popularity or rankings; use charts_get.

tools.name: featuring_history
tools.description:
Use this when you need when and where apps were featured, per app or home shelf, over at most 30 days.
Do not use for current shelf order; use charts_get.

tools.name: listings_profile
tools.description:
Use this when you need a listing profile, or up to 5 (Pro): its app, country availability, ranks, metrics and MCP tools. Stale or refused countries read unknown.
Do not use for discovery; use listings_search.

tools.name: mcp_toolset_get
tools.description:
Use this when you need a tracked app or server's stored MCP tools or changes. at selects a past snapshot; diff_from compares versions.
Do not use for arbitrary URLs; only tracked servers.

tools.name: market_get
tools.description:
Use this when you need store sizes, weekly launches, app kinds or MCP ecosystem statistics.
Do not use for app profiles or rankings.

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Use this when ChatGPT deep research needs listings, apps, tags (query tag:<id>), charts or tracked MCP URLs. Returns typed ids for fetch.
Do not use for rankings or events; use charts_get or changes_list.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description:
Use this when ChatGPT deep research needs a document for an id returned by search: listing, app, tag, chart or MCP toolset.
Do not use for ids outside search results.

tools.name: feedback_send
tools.description: Use this when OpenApps' tools or data fail the user: an error, data the user says is wrong (such as an app bound to the wrong listing), a missing capability, or something confusing. Ask the user before sending a report they did not ask for. It is stored privately with the caller's account and client

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "listings_profile" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "feedback_send" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: listings_search, mcp_toolset_get, search · Private data: fetch, feedback_send · Public sink: feedback_send.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: listings_search, mcp_toolset_get, search · Private data: fetch, feedback_send · Public sink: feedback_send

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
